# FE build identity (git tag + short sha) is generated by an npm pre-hook, never by `netlify.toml` (OBRS-1075)

## Context

A usability report submitted by a customer carries no record of which build produced the page
they were looking at. When a report turns out to describe a bug that was already fixed on a later
build, or a regression only present on one, there is nothing on the report to tell the two apart.

The single source of truth for a version number in this repo is a git tag matching `v*`
(`v1.0.0-alpha`, `v1.1.0-alpha`, …) — there is no version file to keep in sync, because tagging
the repo (`git tag v1.2.0`) is the release itself. `package.json`'s `"version": "0.0.0"` is left
untouched on purpose; it has never been the source and this card does not make it one.

## Decision

A new gitignored module, `src/environments/build-info.ts`, exports:

```ts
export const buildInfo = { appVersion: 'v1.1.0-alpha', buildSha: '3fb8b90' };
```

It is written by `scripts/inject-build-info.mjs`, resolving in this order, **with no fallback**:

1. `buildSha` — `process.env.COMMIT_REF` (set by Netlify) sliced to 7 chars, else
   `git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD`.
2. `appVersion` — `git describe --tags --match v* --abbrev=0`.
3. Either step throwing or resolving empty ⇒ `process.exit(1)` and **no file is written**.
   Never `'unknown'`, `''`, `'0.0.0'`, or `'dev'` — a build stamped with a fake identity is worse
   than a build that refuses to ship, because the fake value looks trustworthy on the report.

`FooterComponent` exposes `readonly build = buildInfo` and renders it in `.copyright-container`
(`HOME.FOOTER.BUILD_VERSION`) — the one place on every customer-facing page that is guaranteed
reachable, so "what build am I looking at" always has an answer without opening dev tools.
`ReportUsabilityModalComponent.onSubmit()` appends `appVersion`/`buildSha` from the same module to
the `multipart/form-data` payload it already builds, alongside `reporterEmail`.

## `rmSync(OUT)` before either resolve step

`build-info.ts` is gitignored, so `git checkout` / `git pull` never removes a stale one left on
disk from an earlier successful run. Every npm-script lane (`build`, `test`, `e2e:*`, `start*`,
`deploy:sit`) is already protected, because its own `pre*` hook exiting non-zero stops npm from
running the main script. But several `playwright.*.config.ts` `webServer` entries invoke
`npx ng serve` / `npx ng test` directly, which skips npm hooks entirely. Without deleting the old
output first, a generator failure on one of those bypass lanes would silently compile against
*last run's* values with no error at all — a stale, undetectable build identity.

Deleting the output before resolving turns that same failure into a loud
`TS2307: Cannot find module './build-info'` on every lane, bypass or not. Proven in
`scripts/check-inject-build-info.mjs` case 4: a fake `build-info.ts` is written first, then
`generate()` is run in a failing environment, and the fake file must be gone afterwards, not just
the process exit code being non-zero.

## Why the npm pre-hook, not `netlify.toml`

`scripts/check-netlify-ignore.mjs` asserts `netlify.toml`'s `[build].command` byte-identical to a
pinned string, because the value configured in the Netlify UI is a *different* string that never
runs `scripts/inject-sit-env.js`. Adding the generator there would only run on the Netlify UI's
path, not the pinned one this repo actually tests. Every lane that builds, tests, or serves the
app already runs through an `npm run <script>` call, so wiring the generator into that script's
`pre<name>` hook (the same mechanism `scripts/check-local-env.mjs` already uses) reaches every
lane without touching `netlify.toml` at all:

| script | pre-hook now runs |
| --- | --- |
| `build`, `build:sit`, `build:prod` | `prebuild`, `prebuild:sit`, `prebuild:prod` |
| `test` | `pretest` (new) |
| `start*` (4 variants) | `prestart*` |
| `e2e*` (4 variants) | `pree2e*` |
| `deploy:sit` | `predeploy:sit` |

## Why no fallback

Business rule: the recorded value must be the build the reporter actually saw, or nothing.
A default like `'dev'` or `'0.0.0'` cannot be distinguished from a real value on the report, so a
broken generator would silently poison every report filed against it — the exact failure mode
this card exists to prevent. Failing the build is the safe direction: it is loud on the machine
that broke, at the moment it broke.

## Consequences

- A checkout or CI job with no reachable `v*` tag, or running outside a git working tree, cannot
  build, test, or serve the app until that is fixed. This is intentional (AC-6).
- `.git` must be present at build time for `git describe`/`git rev-parse` to resolve; this is
  already true for every lane in this repo (local checkouts, Netlify's own clone — see
  `scripts/netlify-ignore.mjs`, which already shells out to `git` with full history).
- `build-info.ts` is regenerated on every build/test/e2e/start invocation; it is never checked in
  and never read from a stale copy left by a different branch.
